title: Evidence provenance & SIEM export playbook
summary: A practical runbook for capturing evidence provenance across RBAC v2 actions, preparing audited artifacts for automated SIEM export, and ensuring chain-of-custody for security incidents. Designed for on-call responders and investigators to reduce manual steps and avoid telemetry gaps.
prerequisites: Access to the security audit index (read) and evidence-store (write)
RBAC v2 service policy templates available in repo: infra/rbac/policies
SIEM exporter service running in prod-us-east-1 and staging-us-west-2
On-call roster and escalation contacts up-to-date in PagerDuty
runbook_steps: 1) Triage & declare incident: Confirm scope and severity. Open JIRA incident JIRA-SEC-xxxxx and post initial summary to #sec-oncall. Capture initial hypothesis and affected resources.

2) Snapshot RBAC state: Run 'rbacctl export --tx-id=auto --format=ndjson > /tmp/rbac-snapshot.ndjson' and store to the evidence-store path for the incident with a metadata record. Tag snapshot with incident id and oncall user.

3) Capture audit stream window: Identify the audit index time-range (t0..t1) around the event. If using streaming export, spin up temporary export job: 'siem-exporter create --index=audit-events --start=t0 --end=t1 --out=/tmp/audit-window.ndjson'. Ensure job receives a request_id for provenance.
4) Freeze volatile artifacts: For affected VMs/containers, request snapshot via infra-sre: 'snapshot-request --target <resource> --incident JIRA-SEC-xxxxx'. Record snapshot hash in evidence metadata.

5) Hash & sign evidence: For every artifact (rbac snapshot, audit window, kernel logs), compute SHA256 and sign using the incident key in the evidence-store. Record signer and timestamp in the evidence metadata entry.

6) Ingest to evidence-store: Upload artifacts to s3://redwood-evidence/<incident>/ and create a manifest file with fields: artifact_name, artifact_type, sha256, signer, created_by, created_at, origin_request_id. Persist manifest to the audit index as a documented event.

7) Create SIEM export bundle: Use the exporter tool to map audit events to the agreed schema (see 'siem_mapping_examples' below). Tag the bundle with the incident id and include a link to the manifest. Validate the bundle against ECS-style schema before sending.

8) Notify downstream: Post a summary to #sec-ops and to the compliance mailbox with links to evidence manifest and the SIEM bundle. Attach minimal context (who, what, when) and indicate retention class.

9) Lock changes to RBAC: If necessary, apply temporary deny policy using RBAC v2 emergency role 'sec-isolate' and record the policy change as an auditable action. Use canary rollout to avoid broad disruption.

10) Monitor and iterate: Keep a rolling export every 30 minutes for the first 6 hours, then hourly for the next 48 hours. Add automated regression alerts for replayed attacker behaviors and for audit-ingest failures.
11) Transition to postmortem: After containment, collect final artifacts, verify signatures, and hand off to the postmortem owner. Close the temporary SIEM jobs and mark evidence bundles as final.
12) Legal / compliance hold: If required, add retention lock via compliance-ops so artifacts cannot be deleted until sign-off. Record the hold in the incident JIRA ticket.

13) Clean-up: Remove ephemeral keys used to sign artifacts, revoke short-lived export credentials, and rotate exporter service tokens per secret rotation policy. Note actions in the incident timeline.
escalation_matrix: If evidence-store upload fails: page infra-sre -> escalation contact (PagerDuty), attach full exporter logs
If SIEM mapping validation fails: page platform-observability and sec-telemetry lead; include failing sample and mapping diff
If RBAC emergency policy causes service disruption: roll back immediately and notify platform-eng leads within 15 min
If chain-of-custody disputed: escalate to compliance-ops and legal; freeze deletions and preserve all related snapshots
evidence_handling_checklist: Always compute and record SHA256 for every artifact
Record actor.principal and actor.role for actions that generated evidence
Include origin_request_id linking export job -> audit events -> resource snapshots
Store timestamp in UTC and include monotonic tx_id when available
Keep at least two geographically separated copies for P1 incidents
Never modify original artifact; only append signed manifest entries
Mark retention_class in manifest (standard | longterm-legal | ephemeral)
Document any data redaction and the redaction rationale in manifest
siem_mapping_examples: Target format: ECS-like JSON with normalized fields. Minimal mapping keys below:
Validation: run 'siem-exporter validate --file=/tmp/siem-bundle.json' and expect zero schema errors before upload
audit_log_schema_notes: Recommended core fields for RBAC v2 audit events:
- tx_id (monotonic transaction id or request id)
- action (allowed values: policy.create, policy.modify, policy.delete, authz.check, token.issue, token.revoke)
- pre_state_hash and post_state_hash (when policy change occurs)
- evidence_refs (list of artifact URIs associated with the event)
Note: include a 'provenance' section as free-form tags when evidence is externally supplied (third-party scans, customer reports).
rbac_considerations: Emergency role pattern: 'sec-isolate' should be scoped narrowly and require two approvers for rollout
Audit retention: keep policy-change events for 2 years (default) and for 7+ years if marked legal-hold
Least-privilege principle: record the minimal effective role set in actor.role rather than all possible groups
Service-to-service actions: include both caller_service and called_service when available
Change surges: add an anomaly flag when policy-change rate > 3x baseline in 1 minute window
rollback_and_postmortem_steps: When incident is stabilized, prepare final artifact set and validate signatures
Create postmortem doc using template POSTMORTEM-SEC-BASE in Confluence and link to incident ticket
Populate timeline with evidentiary references (manifest URIs) and attach SIEM bundle
Identify root cause and remediation actions; assign owners and SLAs
Update RBAC policy templates and exporter mappings as needed and create follow-up Jira tasks
Schedule a cross-team review (security, platform, compliance) within 10 business days
notes_and_open_questions: Q: Should evidence manifests include full user agent strings? Trade-off between telemetry value and PII exposure.
Q: Do we standardize on 'sha256:' prefix in manifest or leave raw hex? Current tooling prefers 'sha256:abcdef...'.
Action: platform-observability to add a SIEM exporter dry-run mode that produces pre-signed upload URLs for the evidence-store
Action: Legal to sign off on 7-year retention class wording for cross-border incidents (EU customers)
